paper.central_claim: A bi-level multi-agent system (orchestrator + parallel workers on a shared workboard) jointly evolves decomposition skills and execution skills through a run-verify-reflect loop over external memory (no weight updates), reaching SOTA on WideSearch (Avg@4 SR 38.50, Row F1 63.53, Item F1 80.12) and 73.0 on XBench-DeepSearch.
paper.title: Web2BigTable: A Bi-Level Multi-Agent LLM System for Internet-Scale Information Search and Extraction

evidence.quote: sets a new state of the art on WideSearch, reaching an Avg@4 Success Rate of 38.50
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim; author-reported.

evidence.quote: but often rely on fixed or weakly adaptive planning strategies, with limited feedback from downstream execution to upstream decomposition
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: decomposition is fixed or weakly adaptive in hierarchical/workflow-search neighbours.

evidence.quote: yet this adaptation has largely been studied at a single level, without jointly refining how tasks are decomposed and how sub-tasks are solved.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated residue vs single-level self-evolving agents (SAMULE, EvolveR, SAGE, SkillRL, Memento-Skills).

evidence.quote: we synthesise a set of 20 queries by perturbing task parameters (e.g., entity counts or time ranges) to avoid overlap with the original benchmark, and use these to learn the orchestrator’s decomposition skills via the run-verify-reflect pipeline.
evidence.support_explanation: Training queries are perturbations of benchmark tasks (near-template overlap with test not audited); gold tables for them are required.

evidence.quote: the unmodified 200 tasks serve as the held-out test set.
evidence.support_explanation: Train/test split with frozen skills; test = the full original benchmark.

evidence.quote: Prior skills are never overwritten, so updates are monotone additions.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention rule is append-only: no acceptance test, merge, forgetting, rollback or versioned replacement.

evidence.quote: Training queries are clustered by structural decomposition pattern rather than semantic topic, typically yielding clusters such as split-by-entity and split-by-time-period
evidence.support_explanation: Reflection groups failures by structural pattern, then synthesises a generalisable decomposition skill per cluster plus a router skill.

evidence.quote: To rigorously prevent overfitting, these skills are constrained to use only structural placeholders.
evidence.support_explanation: Overfitting guard by construction; effectiveness untested (no skill-level held-out check).

evidence.quote: w/o learned orch. skills 7.00 45.23 62.87 41.0
evidence.support_explanation: Store-off ablation on same backbones: SR 38.50 -> 7.00, Item F1 80.12 -> 62.87, XBench 73.0 -> 41.0.
Reference row for ablation.
Workboard-off ablation (short-term coordination, not retained across tasks).

evidence.quote: w/o worker skill evolution 33.00 59.67 76.38 64.0
evidence.support_explanation: Described as losing the ability to discover cloud skills or repair failures, i.e. also disables use of the 8,000-skill catalogue, not just evolved skills.

evidence.quote: No reflection, verification, or memory update is performed
evidence.support_explanation: Inference phase is read-only by claim.

evidence.quote: module leverages the worker’s LLM to synthesise a novel skill on demand

evidence.quote: No post-processing (summarisation, deduplication, etc.) is applied: correctness is expected to emerge directly from the decomposition design.
evidence.support_explanation: Contradicted by the case study ('after deduplication and aggregation').

evidence.quote: Workers collectively retrieve 653 raw rows; after deduplication and aggregation, 556 unique rows are submitted for evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Aggregation includes deduplication, contradicting Sec 2.4.1.

evidence.quote: Baseline results are sourced from published reports.
evidence.support_explanation: XBench baselines are not re-run under the same setup; WideSearch baselines use earlier-generation LLMs.

evidence.quote: Each system is run four times independently on the test set.
evidence.support_explanation: Avg@4 and Max@4 reported; no SD/CI; training (skill learning) is run once.

evidence.quote: GPT-5 mini (single agent) 4.00 22.10 33.28 35.0
evidence.support_explanation: Single-agent backbone baseline: SR 4.00, Item F1 33.28, XBench 35.0 vs framework 38.50/80.12/73.0; not compute-matched.

evidence.quote: We deliberately pair two lightweight, cost-efficient models with high rate limits to demonstrate that performance stems from framework design rather than backbone capability
evidence.support_explanation: Cost-efficiency asserted but no token, call, time or dollar figures anywhere in the read text.

evidence.quote: so the 6 to 8 point gap between these rows and the officially reported scores (for example, 64.0 versus 72.0 for Minimax-M2) most likely reflects undocumented setup differences rather than capability gaps in the underlying models.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' own re-evaluations of baselines are 6-8 points below published ones; they pick published numbers as the primary comparison.

evidence.quote: Web2BigTable achieves 73.0 accuracy, surpassing all baselines including frontier proprietary systems such as Minimax-M2 and MiroFlow (both at 72.0).
evidence.support_explanation: One-point margin on a ~100-task benchmark, single run; not distinguishable from noise.

evidence.quote: accuracy improves from 41.0 (without learned skills) to 73.0 following strategy learning, a gain of 32.0 points from 20 synthesised training queries.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained-skill effect on a held-out benchmark; training queries are benchmark-specific modifications.

evidence.locator: Appendix C Case A skill text
evidence.quote: If any entity has >80 expected items, split further by region.
evidence.support_explanation: Learned skill content is inspectable and specific (shown for three tasks), supporting the human-readable-memory claim; skill count/size not reported.

evidence.quote: Should a skill execution terminate in failure, the worker initiates an autonomous reflection loop. The error trace and the current skill code are supplied to the LLM to synthesise a corrected iteration, subjected to strict AST validation before replacing the original.
evidence.support_explanation: Worker skill repair is gated by AST validity only, not by outcome improvement.

evidence.quote: Web2BigTable acquires both banks autonomously through a dedicated training phase that runs on a small split of queries paired with gold-standard tables, so that extraction quality can be evaluated objectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback signal is a privileged gold table available only at training; construction of gold tables for synthesised queries not described.

evidence.quote: On each benchmark, skills are learned from 20 benchmark-specific training queries and frozen prior to test-time evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Skills are learned per benchmark; no cross-benchmark transfer of a learned skill bank is shown.

evidence.quote: executing ReAct loops with access to web search, file operations, shell commands, and a shared library comprising over 8,000 cloud skills.
evidence.support_explanation: Resource context for cost/budget: up to 10 parallel workers plus a large skill catalogue.

evidence.quote: Across all three metric categories, existing multi-agent frameworks plateau below 6 SR, 39 Row F1, and 63 Item F1 despite employing strictly stronger backbone LLMs (o3-high, Claude Sonnet 4).
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline multi-agent frameworks are earlier-generation and differently configured; no matched budget or matched backbone.

gap.author_gap: Web-to-table (wide) search needs broad, consistent coverage; monolithic agents saturate context, and hierarchical/workflow-search frameworks use fixed or weakly adaptive decomposition with little feedback from execution to decomposition; self-evolving agents adapt at only one level.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and demonstrated: case studies show default time-window decomposition mixes tours/product lines and causes coverage failure (234 of 534 rows retrieved), which the learned skill fixes. The learned object (decomposition strategy) is clearly distinct from evolved execution skills. Nearest neighbours (automated workflow search, Memento-Skills, SAGE, SkillRL, G-Memory) are named but not compared experimentally; the only learned-decomposition comparator is the authors' own no-skill ablation.
gap.lineage: ReAct/deep research agents -> hierarchical multi-agent decomposition and automated workflow search (AFlow-like) -> skill-library self-evolving agents (Memento-Skills, SAGE) -> bi-level decomposition+execution skill learning with shared workboard.
gap.closest_adjacent: Memento-Skills (supplies the worker agent), automated workflow search, EvolveR/SAMULE reflection; none run as baselines.
gap.residue: Learning how to decompose (which axis to split a wide task on) from gold-referenced failures, rather than hand-set heuristics.
gap.stakes: WideSearch success rates of 0-5% for all prior systems (author table).
gap.method_response: Reflect over failure clusters into router + decomposition skills; shared workboard for coordination.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether a hand-written decomposition skill gives the same gain; transfer of learned skills across benchmarks; label-free (no gold) skill learning; cost.
gap.unresolved: Head-to-head with learned-decomposition neighbours; role of benchmark-specific training queries.

claims.text: Learned orchestrator decomposition skills are the primary driver of the gain.
claims.setting: WideSearch 200 tasks (Avg@4) and XBench-DeepSearch; GPT-5 mini orchestrator + Gemini 3 Flash workers; skills learned from 20 benchmark-specific queries
claims.baseline_control: Same system without learned orchestrator skills (generic LLM decomposition)
claims.selection_vs_test: Training = 20 perturbed queries; test = unmodified benchmark; skills frozen
claims.result_denominator: SR 38.50 vs 7.00; Row F1 63.53 vs 45.23; Item F1 80.12 vs 62.87; XBench 73.0 vs 41.0; Avg@4 over 4 inference runs, one skill-learning run
claims.counterevidence: Training queries derived from benchmark tasks (overlap not audited); no hand-written decomposition skill baseline; no variance across skill-learning runs
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported: skills learned from 20 benchmark-derived queries and frozen yield large gains over a skill-less orchestrator on the same benchmark family.

claims.text: SOTA on WideSearch and 73.0 on XBench-DeepSearch.
claims.baseline_control: Published single-agent, end-to-end and multi-agent baselines with earlier-generation LLMs; XBench published numbers
claims.result_denominator: SR 38.50 vs 5.10 second best; XBench 73.0 vs 72.0
claims.counterevidence: Baselines not run under matched backbone, budget or tool setup; 1-point XBench margin on ~100 tasks, single run
claims.allowed_conclusion: Large WideSearch margin over published baselines is credible in direction; XBench 'surpassing all baselines' is not distinguishable from ties.

claims.text: Workboard coordination enables dynamic gap recovery.
claims.counterevidence: Mechanism (redundancy avoidance, strategy adaptation) not directly measured
claims.allowed_conclusion: Workboard removal hurts; specific coordination behaviours are not verified.

claims.text: Worker skill evolution gives complementary gains.
claims.counterevidence: Ablation also removes catalogue skill discovery; runtime creation persists at inference
claims.allowed_conclusion: Skill discovery/repair tooling helps; contribution of evolved (retained) worker skills is not isolated.

claims.text: Gain comes from the framework, not the backbone LLMs.
claims.counterevidence: Compute and tool access (10 workers, 8,000 skills) not matched
claims.allowed_conclusion: Framework beats same-backbone single agents at unreported, larger cost.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: decomposition skills learned once from 20 benchmark-derived gold-referenced queries and frozen produced a large held-out gain over the same system with generic decomposition (WideSearch SR 7.0 -> 38.5; XBench 41.0 -> 73.0). Not shown: independence from the training-test template overlap, transfer across benchmarks, improver level, matched cost, or that worker-skill evolution (vs catalogue use) matters.
assessment.unresolved: Contamination of perturbed training queries; hand-written-skill baseline; cost; variance of skill learning; worker-evolution isolation.

G.reason: Specific, demonstrated bottleneck (fixed decomposition axis yields coverage gaps; case studies show 234/534 rows vs 556) and a distinct changed object (orchestrator strategy) relative to single-level self-evolving agents. Nearest neighbours are named but not experimentally contrasted, so below 4.

M.reason: Verify-against-gold, structural clustering of failures, placeholder-constrained skill synthesis and a router skill form a coherent, reconstructable response to the coverage gap, with inspectable skill text. Not 4: no analysis of why learned skills should beat a human-written decomposition prompt and worker-level evolution rationale is thin.

X.reason: Training/inference split, frozen reads and router are clear, but retention is append-only with no acceptance gate, versioned replacement, conflict handling or forgetting; skill count unreported; contradictions (runtime skill creation at 'read-only' inference; 'no deduplication' vs deduplication in case studies).

E.measurement.reason: Uses established benchmarks with strict success rate plus row/item F1 and gold tables; includes backbone single-agent baselines. LLM-as-judge for XBench and free-text cells and baselines taken from heterogeneous published setups remain concerns.

E.causality.reason: Large store-off ablation of the retained orchestrator skills on two benchmarks and same-backbone single-agent comparisons are the key controls. Missing: hand-written decomposition skill, gate-off/alternative optimizer, compute-matched baselines, and an unconfounded worker-evolution ablation.

E.holdout.reason: Frozen skills evaluated on the unmodified benchmark is the right design, but training queries are perturbations of that benchmark with no overlap audit, skills are learned per benchmark, and no transfer to another task family is shown.

E.statistics.reason: Four independent inference runs with Avg@4 and Max@4 and per-language splits give some spread information, but no SD/CI, one skill-learning run, and XBench ~100 tasks single run with 1-point claims.

E.cost.reason: 'Cost-efficient' is asserted, but no tokens, calls, wall-clock, dollars or training-cost figures are reported for 10 parallel workers, reflection LLMs, or skill retrieval.

rationale: 编排器分解技能经金标反思写入SKILL.md并冻结，存储关闭对照效应很大，设计清晰；但训练题由基准扰动生成未审计、仅追加无门控、基线与成本不匹配且成本未报。
